name: Private credit stress
summary: Fitch's US private credit default rate eased to 6.2% in October; nontraded BDCs still limit redemptions to 5% a quarter
state: Fitch data reported on 17 Nov show the trailing 12-month US private credit default rate eased to 6.2% in October from 6.3% in September, with 10.7% for borrowers with EBITDA under $25m and 9.8% in industrials (Investment Executive). Fitch said in October that nontraded BDCs faced third-quarter redemption requests averaging 9.8% of shares against a 5% quarterly cap (InvestmentNews). Searches on 19 Nov found no simultaneous gating by several large funds, forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Mainly affects holders of nontraded BDCs and private credit funds, whose withdrawals are capped at 5% a quarter, and mid-sized firms that borrow from these lenders. Defaults tend to show up first in smaller and industrial borrowers.
rubric_hit: Watch: listed funds limiting redemptions (5% quarterly cap vs 9.8% requested) and 6.2% default rate; no multi-fund gating or bank losses (Alert)

sources.title: Investment Executive — U.S. private credit defaults ease in October: Fitch
InvestmentNews — Pace of investors selling nontraded BDCs slows but remains significant, says Fitch

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
